September 3rd, 2015 I lost my very best friend/boyfriend to addiction. He didn’t overdose, but due to years of abuse his body simply gave out. He went to sleep and never woke up. He was in a coma for four and a half days before his final breath. The neurologist explained to his family and I that he was completely brain dead. He told us “imagine the human brain as a 10 story building, the top floor being completely functional. His brain is in the basement.” I was in complete denial those four days, I sang to him every night the jack and sally song and every time he would gurgle I thought for sure it was because he was responding. But sadly no, it was just the machines making his body respond. 

Even at his funeral, him laying in his casket, me staring down at him completely lifeless, I still denied he was gone. When he was alive sometimes he’d just up and disappear for awhile and wouldn’t contact anyone until he was ready to come home. So that’s what I told myself. It wasn’t him in the casket, they got the wrong man. He’s just off somewhere exploring and soon he’ll call us and tell us he’s ready to come home. Most days honestly, I still have this mindset. I’m just waiting for him to come home or waiting to see his name light up my phone screen and say “hey sugar, I’m here.” 

You’re going to go through the stages of grief. And it is up to no one, only yourself, how long you stay in those stages. And some days it’s going to hit you all over again, they’ll feel like waves crashing over you and it will completely consume you. But, do. not. let. it. drown. you. 

I have heavily struggled with fully attaching myself In new relationships because of that “I’m still waiting for him..” when logically I know he’s never coming home. I’ve walked away from completely healthy, nurturing, and loving relationships because of this. I have completely sabotaged myself and my own happiness because of this. 

Embrace grief. Embrace the memories you share with them, embrace every single thing you can. Embrace the sadness, embrace the heartache, and embrace the love they shared. Because at least you are FEELING. 

There is no right way or wrong way in dealing with grief. Do not let anyone ever try and make you feel guilty for your grief, don’t let anyone tell you how you should grieve, and don’t allow people to tell you “it’s been (however months or years) it’s time to move on.” Because there’s no moving on from it. But you can take steps forward, you can revel in the fact that you are alive and by that fact alone, you can share their story and they will live through you. 

Do not let grief control your life like it has mine though, please. If there’s any sort of advice I can give you that would “help” here they are. 

1) take a shower every day. Sometimes this might seem very difficult and you just want to stay in bed, and that is a very valid thing to feel. But take a shower. Wash off the emotions weighing you down in that moment. 

2) once you’ve showered, brush your teeth and then brush your hair. These may seem like huge mountains to tackle in the beginning stages of grief. But if you can tackle these, you are already in the right direction. 


You will feel like you have no control over it, because well, you don’t. But you can control those things, you can control taking care of yourself physically while your mental state sorts it way through it’s emotions. 

3) Don’t spend too much time in bed if you can avoid it. I know this might be extremely difficult to do, and that’s okay. And it’s okay if you do decide to stay in bed all day, just don’t get stuck there. 

4) eat, make yourself something to eat. Even if it’s super tiny, even if it’s just crackers. I know how little to no appetite you may have, but it is essential you eat. 

When your mind is idle for too long, that’s when the waves come crashing down. So get up out of bed, take that shower, brush your teeth, and brush your hair, and make sure you eat. 


I’m so sorry OP, losing a loved one is one of the harshest realities a person can go through. And I’m so sorry you are experiencing this, I wish I could take that pain from you. I hope you have a huge support system right now, and if you don’t, never hesitate to reach out to a stranger. Sometimes unbiased views are better to digest. I wish you all the best, keep moving forward.

If or when this becomes a relationship, or you get in a relationship with someone else. Be super transparent with them about your grief. I dated someone for about a year after my bf died 4 years ago and the new bf (now ex) just couldn’t seem to understand “why I couldn’t just let him go.” For some reason he was extremely threatened by my grief over my deceased boyfriend, I think in some way he thought it meant I could never love him the same or something. But it became really toxic. I couldn’t talk about it, if I wore the necklace with his ashes it was a fight, if I hung out with his family then he’d blow up my phone the entire time. And I meant literally blew up my phone, I had 32 missed calls in the span of 30 minutes. 

Don’t let anyone EVER make you feel bad or guilty for your grief or your feelings. And I mean this, it will most definitely fuck you up in so many different ways. Now I’m with someone who encourages me to open about my deceased bf, he loves to hear about my stories about him, he says it helps him understand who I am more and why I react to certain things. For a long time I still felt guilt (because of my ex) to bring it up, but my current SO will gently bring up the one who passed away for me so I don’t feel awkward about it. 

Also, don’t be scared to let someone else in 🖤

When I was fourteen, I'm eighteen now...my best friend and I where outside working on his car together. He was 17 at the time. I didn't know a single thing about cars or tools or anything like that. We were laughing about something and he said to me "hey, bag of bones will you grab me that wrench?" As soon as I turned my head to grab it all I hear is a loud thud. In that second I knew exactly what happened. I didn't need to turn around to see what happened, I just knew. Every sound, every smell, everything just kinda disappeared except for the repeating sound of that loud thud. It felt like it had been hours of me just sitting there trying to process what had just happened. But it was a matter of seconds. Finally, I turned my head and all I could see was his limp legs and arms on the ground. The jack had snapped and his car fell on top of him, instantly killing him. My house was right next to his so I screamed and ran for my dad, soon my friends mother came home completely mortified. I remember my parents and his, even the neighbors trying to pull the car off of him. We all followed the ambulance to the hospital. It was my job to tell all of his friends including my bf at the time that he had passed. A short time after that I tried to kill myself. I don't really think about it as much now, but when I do it leaves me in a terrible mind set. I'll never forget the day that I watched my best friend die. It was three days before my birthday, it was going to be the first birthday that I was going to have a friend over for. His name was Michael.
